title: VLAN Pruning Concept
description: Understand why VLAN pruning matters and how to control which VLANs cross a trunk.
scenario: Understand why VLAN pruning matters and how to control which VLANs cross a trunk.

concepts.title: What is VLAN Pruning?
concepts.body: VLAN pruning prevents unnecessary VLAN traffic from crossing trunk links. A trunk only forwards frames for VLANs that actually exist on the far end.
concepts.code:
Trunk Gi0/1: carries VLANs 1-4094 by default
After pruning: only VLANs 10-20 cross

concepts.title: Manual Pruning with Allowed VLANs
concepts.body: On Cisco IOS, use "switchport trunk allowed vlan" to manually prune. Use "add" to keep existing allowed VLANs.
concepts.code:
SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan 10-20
SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 30

concepts.title: Restoring All VLANs
concepts.body: Use the keyword "all" to restore the default of carrying every VLAN over the trunk.
concepts.code: SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan all

concepts.title: Why Prune?
concepts.body: Pruning reduces unnecessary broadcasts, multicasts, and inefficiency over trunk links. It is especially useful on links to switches/distribution layers that do not need every VLAN.
concepts.code: Less unnecessary traffic → better use of trunk bandwidth
